fields.statement: At 6e29d497, `go test -trimpath -count=1 ./internal/api -run 'TestLearnedLimit' -v` passes. TestLearnedLimitRatchets checks raiseLearned directly. TestLearnedLimitRatchetsAtPoll drives daemonProj.prepare and saveState with a fake ctx.Now and fake token records (holdFakeRecords), then reads the learned limits back with daemon.ReadState. It covers four cases. Use 1500 over a learned 1000 with no hit is saved as 1500 and keeps the old hit time. Use under a learned 2000 leaves it. A window holding a weekly hit saves the 1500 used at the hit, not the 2200 used since, with the new hit time. After the limit is raised to 1500, a later week's hit at 1200 use moves it down to 1200, and with rhiza.daemon.usage.weekly=42 set, usageLimit still returns 42. The diff calls learnLimits before ratchetLimits in prepare. ratchetLimits leaves alone any kind whose window holds a hit of that kind, and it never touches settings. gofmt and go vet on internal/api are clean. All three findings from attempt 1 are addressed. The wider run `-run 'TestLimitHit|TestUsage|TestLearn'` passes from a worktree outside ~/code. Under ~/code, TestUsageWindowsHitKinds fails: it predates this leaf and is unchanged by it, and it reads leaked usage hits from the ~/code root's state.
